title: Part A: Trace Storage (Steps 1-7)
Phase B: Row selection checkbox slide-in
No CLI flag to evaluate against user's own documentation
description: The agent-evals CLI hardcodes doc_tree loading via load_doc_tree_for_source() which only supports the built-in 56-file sample fixture or pre-prepared dataset adapters. There is no --docs or --local flag to point at real user documentation. The end-to-end workflow (scan docs with agent-index → evaluate with agent-evals) requires users to either: (1) manually create a dataset adapter, or (2) hack the source.py routing. Need: a --docs <path> flag that calls agent_index.scanner.scan_local(), applies tier assignment, and passes the resulting DocTree to the evaluation runner. This is the critical missing link between the two packages.

title: Report aggregator CI uses z=1.96 instead of t-distribution for small sample sizes
Add configuration/setup and migration task types
description: The 11 task types miss two of the most common real-world agent documentation tasks: (1) CONFIGURATION TASKS: 'How do I configure X with settings Y and Z?' — tests whether the agent can synthesize a complete config file from scattered doc fragments, scored by config validity + completeness. (2) MIGRATION/UPGRADE TASKS: 'Upgrade from v2 to v3' — tests whether the agent can identify breaking changes, deprecated features, and produce a migration plan, scored by change coverage + correctness. (3) API INTEGRATION TASKS: 'Write code that calls the Widget API with auth' — tests end-to-end integration synthesis from API docs. These are the tasks where documentation format matters MOST because they require synthesizing information from multiple doc sections. The existing code_generation type is too generic to capture config/migration-specific patterns.

title: Add document freshness/staleness simulation
description: Real documentation is partially stale — some pages are current, some are months or years old, some are contradictory across versions. The temporal axis (10) only adds timestamps/version markers to docs but doesn't simulate the INFORMATION DECAY problem. Need: (1) inject deliberate version conflicts (v2 docs still present alongside v3), (2) test whether formats that emphasize recency help agents prefer newer info, (3) measure 'staleness tolerance' per format — how much outdated content can exist before accuracy drops, (4) simulate 'docs drift' where 20% of content is subtly wrong (not just deprecated). This matters because every real documentation corpus has staleness issues and the right format should help agents navigate them.

title: No 'apply optimal' workflow from Taguchi results to agent-index config
description: After running a Taguchi pipeline and identifying optimal factor levels (e.g., structure-3tier, metadata-with-summary, format-yaml), there is no automated way to translate those findings into an agent-index IndexConfig that implements those choices. The pipeline returns final_optimal as a dict of factor→level mappings, but users must manually: (1) interpret variant names back to config parameters, (2) write an agent-index.yaml by hand, (3) re-run agent-index with those settings. Need: an 'apply' command or export function that maps Taguchi optimal levels to IndexConfig fields (tier count, metadata inclusion, output format, etc.) and generates a ready-to-use agent-index.yaml.

title: Add actionable recommendations engine from Taguchi results
description: The pipeline produces S/N ratios, ANOVA tables, and optimal configurations, but no human-readable actionable guidance. A technical writer looking at 'axis_3: yaml, axis_1: 3tier, axis_8: section' doesn't know what to DO. Need: (1) natural language recommendation generator: 'Use 3-tier hierarchical structure with YAML format and section-level granularity. This combination outperforms alternatives by 23% on retrieval and code generation tasks.', (2) per-audience recommendations (DevRel team, solo dev, enterprise), (3) format-specific style guide generation from winning configurations, (4) confidence-rated recommendations (high/medium/low based on effect sizes and sample size), (5) 'avoid these' anti-patterns from worst-performing configurations. Without this, the framework is a research tool — with this, it becomes a documentation optimization product.
close_reason: Already implemented in codebase - verified against source

title: Progress callback shows no running cost during CLI evaluation
description: The progress callbacks in progress.py (_plain_callback and _rich_callback) only display task_id, variant_name, and score. They do not show accumulated cost, projected total cost, or budget utilization. During a long evaluation run, users have no CLI visibility into spend unless they also run the observatory dashboard. The TrialResult passed to the callback has cost data available. Need: add running cost total and budget percentage to the progress display. E.g., '[####----] 25% (50/200) task_001 | scale_50 | 0.85 | $0.42/$2.00 (21%)'.

title: Add code block formatting axis
description: No axis tests how CODE BLOCKS within documentation affect agent performance. Real docs are full of code examples. Need new axis testing: (1) code block density (no examples, inline only, full examples per section), (2) code block language tagging (```python vs untagged), (3) runnable vs pseudo-code examples, (4) code-before-explanation vs explanation-before-code ordering, (5) import statement inclusion/exclusion, (6) error handling in examples (complete vs minimal). This interacts heavily with code_generation and agentic task types. Currently the fixture docs have some code but it's not systematically varied as a treatment.

title: Add heading depth and semantic structure axis
description: The structure axis (1) tests flat/2tier/3tier/4tier but doesn't test HEADING SEMANTICS — how heading text itself affects navigation. Need new axis: (1) heading verbosity (terse 'Config' vs descriptive 'Database Configuration Options'), (2) heading hierarchy depth (2 levels vs 6 levels for same content), (3) numbered vs unnumbered headings, (4) question-style headings ('How do I configure X?') vs noun-style ('Configuration'), (5) heading-as-TOC (headings that preview their content) vs heading-as-label. LLMs use headings as primary navigation cues — this is likely a high-impact untested dimension.

title: Full-config.yaml example missing Taguchi/pipeline/observatory options
description: The examples/full-config.yaml only documents basic evaluation options (LLM settings, scope, execution, cost control, output). It is missing documentation for 15+ config keys that the CLI supports: mode (taguchi), models (multi-model list), pipeline (auto/semi), quality_type (larger_is_better/smaller_is_better/nominal_is_best), top_k, alpha, oa_type, report (html/md/both), store_traces, dashboard, dashboard_port, source (dataset selection), budget, model_budgets, resume, resume_pipeline. Users have no YAML reference for the advanced DOE/pipeline features and must read source code or CLI --help to discover them.

title: Phase B: Row hover elevation
Add multi-corpus generalization validation framework
description: The framework can't answer the fundamental question: 'Do these format recommendations work for MY docs, or only for YOUR test corpus?' Need: (1) corpus fingerprinting — characterize a doc corpus by size, complexity, code density, domain, language, (2) results portability analysis — measure how well Taguchi rankings from corpus A predict performance on corpus B, (3) conditional recommendations — 'for API-heavy docs, prefer X; for tutorial-heavy docs, prefer Y', (4) user-supplied corpus adapter — let someone plug in their own docs and get personalized recommendations. This requires both the real dataset work (#46) AND a meta-analysis layer that compares results ACROSS corpora. Without this, every result has an asterisk: 'valid only for our synthetic fixture.'

title: Pipeline resume reconstructs PhaseResult with empty trials, losing cost/token totals
description: When resuming a pipeline (pipeline.py lines 311-323, 344-350, 374-380), completed phases are reconstructed with trials=[] and no cost/token data. This means: (1) PipelineResult.total_trials undercounts (only new phase trials counted), (2) PipelineResult.total_cost undercounts (prior phase costs are 0.0 by default), (3) elapsed_seconds undercounts. The store has all trial data via get_trials(run_id) but it's not loaded during reconstruction. Need: either load trial aggregates from the observatory store (the get_run_summary method has total_cost/trial_count), or persist phase-level cost/token summaries alongside phase_results.

title: Add response calibration and confidence measurement
description: The framework measures ACCURACY but not CALIBRATION — whether the agent knows when it's uncertain. A format that produces 80% accuracy with 95% 'I'm confident' is worse than 80% accuracy with calibrated confidence. Need: (1) extract confidence signals from responses (hedging language, explicit confidence levels), (2) compute Expected Calibration Error (ECE) per variant, (3) measure selective accuracy — if the agent could abstain on uncertain answers, what's its accuracy on remaining ones?, (4) per-variant calibration curves, (5) combine with negative task type to measure whether format helps agent know its limits. This matters enormously for production agents — miscalibrated confidence leads to hallucination that users trust.

title: No CLI command for cross-run comparison
description: The observatory web API has a comparison endpoint (GET /api/compare?ids=run1,run2) but there is no CLI subcommand to compare two runs. Users who want to compare runs without launching the dashboard have no option. Need: an 'agent-evals compare <run_id_1> <run_id_2>' CLI command that shows side-by-side variant scores, cost deltas, and statistical significance of score differences between runs. Output as table to terminal or as a report file.

title: algorithmic_compress strips injection markers containing hyphens in marker_id
description: In transform.py:46-48, the regex that preserves injection markers during HTML comment removal uses \w+ which only matches [a-zA-Z0-9_]. Hyphens are not matched. If a user calls inject_into_file(path, content, marker_id='MY-DOCS'), the markers <\!-- MY-DOCS:START --> and <\!-- MY-DOCS:END --> will be stripped by algorithmic_compress because the negative lookahead fails to match the hyphenated ID. Concrete trigger: algorithmic_compress('<\!-- MY-DOCS:START -->\nContent\n<\!-- MY-DOCS:END -->') returns 'Content' with markers deleted. Fix: change \w+ to [\w-]+ in the lookahead pattern.

title: --validate CLI is a no-op: validates freshly-scanned tree against same disk
description: In cli.py:157-193, the --validate workflow does: (1) scan docs fresh from disk, (2) assign tiers, (3) validate that same tree against the same disk. Since the DocTree was just built from the files on disk, missing_files will always be empty (all files exist — we just found them) and stale_entries will always be empty (hashes match — we just computed them). The only check that partially works is extra_files, but even that has issues (see #118). Concrete trigger: delete a doc file, then run 'agent-index --validate --config agent-index.yaml' — it will NOT detect the deletion because it rescans first. The feature should load a previously saved index instead of scanning fresh.

title: Add whitespace and visual density axis
description: No axis tests VISUAL DENSITY of the documentation index. Need: (1) compact vs spacious formatting (single newline vs double newline between entries), (2) indentation depth (2-space vs 4-space vs tabs), (3) separator styles (horizontal rules, blank lines, section markers like '---'), (4) list style (bullet lists vs numbered lists vs no lists), (5) information density per line (one fact per line vs dense paragraphs). This is the lowest-hanging fruit for doc authors — it requires zero content changes, only whitespace/formatting tweaks. LLM tokenizers handle whitespace differently across models, making this potentially model-specific.

title: inject_into_file non-idempotent when appending to file without markers
description: In output.py:338-343, when inject_into_file is called on an existing file that has no markers, content is appended raw without wrapping in START/END markers. The new-file path (line 326) correctly wraps with markers (fixed in commit 42f2c26), but this append path was missed. Concrete trigger: call inject_into_file(path, 'v1') on an existing file without markers, then call inject_into_file(path, 'v2') again — the file now contains both 'v1' and 'v2' appended, with no way to replace. Each subsequent call adds another copy. Fix: wrap appended content with markers, matching the new-file behavior.

title: --validate CLI ignores config file_extensions and ignore_patterns
description: In cli.py:193, the --validate path calls validate_index(doc_tree, scan_path) without passing file_extensions or ignore_patterns from the config. Even though validate_index accepts these params (added in commit 245ef36), the CLI doesn't forward them. Concrete trigger: config has ignore_patterns: ['vendor', 'dist'] but validate uses defaults (['node_modules', '__pycache__', '.git', '.venv']). Files in vendor/ or dist/ appear as false-positive extra_files. Fix: pass config.file_extensions and config.ignore_patterns to validate_index.

title: validate and autodetect rglob lacks symlink loop protection
description: In validate.py:122 (_collect_disk_files) and autodetect.py:194 (_collect_doc_files), both use root.rglob('*') which follows symlinks by default. Unlike scanner.py which has explicit loop detection via visited_dirs set (lines 120-129), these modules have no protection. Concrete trigger: create a symlink loop (e.g., 'ln -s ../docs docs/self') and run auto-detect or validate — rglob will recurse infinitely until hitting OS limits or crashing. Fix: either use rglob with follow_symlinks=False (Python 3.13+) or implement visited-path tracking like the scanner does.

title: Phase C: Premium custom scrollbar
transform_tree incremental skip returns untransformed content on fresh scans
description: In transform.py:296-302, when transform_tree skips a file because its content_hash matches state, it uses the DocFile from the CURRENT doc_tree (new_files[rel_path] = doc). If the current tree came from a fresh scan (not a previously transformed tree), this is the original untransformed content. The state only stores hashes, not transformed content. Concrete trigger: (1) scan + transform tree + save state, (2) scan again (fresh), (3) transform with saved state — skipped files have raw content, not their previously transformed versions. Fix: state needs to store either transformed content or transformed hashes, or the caller must persist and pass the transformed tree.

title: _resolve_strategy silently falls back to passthrough for unrecognized LLM strategy
description: In transform.py:201-207, _resolve_strategy falls through to passthrough when step.type=='llm' but step.strategy is not in _STRATEGY_MAP. The default strategy value on TransformStep is 'default', which has no entry in the map. Concrete trigger: TransformStep(type='llm') or config with transform_steps: [{type: llm}] — silently applies passthrough with no warning or error. User thinks LLM compression is running but gets raw content. Fix: raise ValueError or log a warning when strategy is not found, or add 'default' to _STRATEGY_MAP mapping to a sensible default.

title: Refinement phase (Phase 3) does not compute or report interaction effects
description: Phase 3 (run_refinement in pipeline.py lines 245-281) runs full factorial on top-K factors but only stores raw trial results. It does not: (1) compute 2-way interaction effects between factors, (2) identify which factor combinations are synergistic or antagonistic, (3) report whether the additive model assumption holds, (4) produce any analysis beyond what comes from the orchestrator. The interaction_analysis.py module has Lenth method and half-normal plot code but it's not integrated into Phase 3. The md_renderer.py Taguchi sections (10-14) only render screening phase analysis. Need: Phase 3 should compute interaction effects from the full factorial data and render them in the report.

title: autodetect _classify_file directory names override filename classification
description: In autodetect.py:221-233, _classify_file iterates over ALL path components (directories + filename) left-to-right. The first keyword match wins. Directory names can override more relevant filename-based classification. Concrete trigger: _classify_file('api/getting-started.md') returns 'reference' because 'api' directory matches _REFERENCE_KEYWORDS before the filename 'getting-started' (which would match _REQUIRED_KEYWORDS). Similarly, 'reference/quickstart.md' returns 'reference' not 'required'. Fix: check filename first, or check required keywords across all components before checking reference keywords.

title: --validate CLI renders unused index_content (dead code)
description: In cli.py:186-192, the --validate path computes index_content = render_index(...) but never uses the variable. This is dead code that wastes computation (sorting files, rendering markdown). The variable was likely left over from an earlier design where validate compared rendered output. Fix: remove the sort_files_bluf and render_index calls, or if validation should compare rendered output, actually use index_content.

title: Add comparative benchmark against existing doc optimization methods
description: The framework has no external validation — no comparison to existing documentation quality standards or tools. Need: (1) benchmark against Google's developer documentation style guide recommendations, (2) compare against Divio's documentation system (tutorials/how-to/reference/explanation), (3) test whether Diataxis-style formatting scores differently from ad-hoc formatting, (4) correlate Taguchi-optimal formats with human-rated documentation quality (e.g., ReadTheDocs ratings), (5) A/B test: run the same tasks with human-written 'best practice' docs vs Taguchi-optimized docs. This positions the framework as either validating or challenging industry best practices — either outcome is a publishable result.

title: Add incremental update evaluation (doc change impact analysis)
description: Documentation changes constantly. The framework can't answer: 'If I update one page, how does it affect overall agent performance?' Need: (1) delta-evaluation mode — add/modify/delete one doc and re-score without full re-run, (2) change impact prediction — estimate score impact from doc diffs, (3) regression detection — alert when a doc update degrades performance on specific task types, (4) 'documentation coverage' metric — which areas of the doc corpus contribute most to which task types. This enables CI/CD integration: run agent-evals on doc PRs to catch regressions before merge. Currently the framework only supports full-corpus evaluation.

title: No experiment export/import format for reproducibility sharing
description: While individual runs are stored in the local SQLite observatory DB with full config and trial data, there is no way to export a complete experiment specification as a portable artifact that someone else could reproduce. Need: an 'agent-evals export <run_id>' command that produces a self-contained JSON/YAML bundle including: (1) full EvalRunConfig, (2) model versions used, (3) variant specifications, (4) task IDs and definitions, (5) all trial results, (6) Taguchi analysis if applicable. And a corresponding 'agent-evals import <bundle>' to load into another observatory instance for comparison.
close_reason: Already implemented in codebase - verified against source

title: Add retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) chunking strategy evaluation
description: Most production systems don't inject full docs — they use RAG with embedding-based retrieval. The framework doesn't test how doc FORMAT interacts with CHUNKING STRATEGY. Need: (1) chunking strategies as a new axis (fixed-size, semantic, heading-based, sliding window), (2) test which doc formats chunk well (markdown tables may split badly), (3) measure retrieval recall per variant when using embedding search, (4) test format × chunk-size interactions (e.g., YAML metadata helps with small chunks by preserving context), (5) compare full-injection vs top-K-chunks vs hierarchical retrieval. This bridges the gap between the current 'stuff everything in the prompt' approach and how docs are actually consumed in production RAG pipelines.
close_reason: Superseded by Context Strategy Phase 3 (RAG Mode)

title: CostTracker budget pause not wired to EvalRunner signal handling
description: CostTracker.check_budget() returns True when projected cost exceeds 2x budget, and should_pause() is an alias. However, tracing the runner.py code, the CostTracker is only used in the orchestrator/tracker layer for observatory events (burn_rate_alert, model_budget_exceeded) — it's not wired to actually pause or stop the EvalRunner's ThreadPoolExecutor. The runner has graceful shutdown via SIGINT/SIGTERM but no budget-triggered pause. The budget flag is accepted by the CLI (--budget) but the runner will continue executing trials past the budget limit. Need: wire CostTracker.should_pause() into the runner's trial loop to stop accepting new work when budget is exceeded.

title: Phase C: Provider combobox
Dry-run cost estimation not available for pipeline mode
description: The --dry-run flag in cli.py (lines 612-670) only handles 'full' mode (logs config) and 'taguchi' mode (shows OA design). It does not estimate total cost for pipeline mode (3-phase: screening + confirmation + refinement). Users planning a full DOE pipeline cannot estimate costs before committing. A pipeline dry-run should estimate: Phase 1 cost (OA rows × tasks × screening_reps), Phase 2 cost (1 × tasks × confirmation_reps), Phase 3 cost (top_k^levels × tasks × refinement_reps), and the grand total across all three phases.

title: RobustnessTask missing fuzzy matching despite claiming FactExtraction parity
description:
File: agent-evals/src/agent_evals/tasks/robustness.py

The module docstring says 'Reuses the same scoring logic as FactExtractionTask' but the implementation is missing two fuzzy matching layers present in fact_extraction.py:
- Layer 3: token_set_ratio >= 85 → 0.9
- Layer 4: token_set_ratio >= 70 → 0.7

RobustnessTask only has: exact match → 1.0, alias match → 1.0, keyword fallback → fraction.
FactExtractionTask has: exact → 1.0, alias → 1.0, fuzzy(>=85) → 0.9, fuzzy(>=70) → 0.7, keyword → fraction.

This is ironic: robustness tasks test PERTURBED inputs (typos, paraphrases) where fuzzy matching is most needed, but they have LESS scoring flexibility than the non-perturbed fact_extraction tasks.

Example: expected_answer='CacheConfig default_ttl is 300 seconds', LLM response='The CacheConfig defaults to a TTL of 300 seconds'. In fact_extraction, token_set_ratio would give >=85 → score 0.9. In robustness, exact match fails, aliases fail, keyword fallback gives ~0.6.

Impact: Robustness scores are systematically depressed vs equivalent fact_extraction tasks. This biases Taguchi analysis by making robustness tasks appear artificially harder.
close_reason: Fixed and verified: all 3460 tests pass

title: CodeGenerationTask syntax bonus is Python-only, penalizes non-Python tasks
description:
File: agent-evals/src/agent_evals/tasks/code_generation.py

_check_syntax() uses ast.parse() which only validates Python syntax. Non-Python code generation tasks always get syntax_bonus=0.0, permanently losing 10% of their maximum score (0.1 out of 1.0 in the formula: match_rate*0.7 + (1-violation_rate)*0.2 + syntax_bonus*0.1).

Affected gold standard task: code_generation_018 asks for a YAML pipeline definition. Even a perfect YAML response scores at most 0.9 because ast.parse(yaml_content) raises SyntaxError.

Fix options:
1. Detect language from the code block fence tag (python/yaml/sql/etc) and only validate Python
2. Skip syntax bonus for tasks without a Python-centric entry_point
3. Use a multi-language syntax checker
close_reason: Fixed and verified: all 3460 tests pass

title: XrefDense 'Referenced by:' label is semantically reversed
description:
File: agent-evals/src/agent_evals/variants/xref_dense.py (lines 102-109)

The 'Referenced by:' section is computed by checking which file stems appear in the CURRENT file's content. This finds files that the current file REFERENCES (outgoing links), NOT files that reference the current file (incoming links).

The label should be 'References:' not 'Referenced by:'.

Example: If errors.md mentions 'auth' and 'config' in its content, it renders as:
  errors.md Referenced by: auth.md, config.md
This implies auth.md and config.md reference errors.md, but actually errors.md references them.

The 'See also:' section already partially covers incoming references (files that mention this file's stem), creating further semantic confusion between the two labels.

Impact: Misleading cross-reference labels could confuse the LLM during agentic/retrieval tasks. The LLM might follow 'Referenced by' links expecting incoming references but finding outgoing ones.

title: Negative scorer gives full marks to responses that abstain AND hallucinate
description:
File: agent-evals/src/agent_evals/tasks/negative.py

The scorer uses simple substring matching: any(p in response_lower for p in _FIRM_REFUSAL). It checks for presence of refusal phrases but does NOT check whether the response ALSO provides a confident answer.

A response like 'The timeout is not mentioned explicitly in the documentation, but based on Redis defaults it is likely 60 seconds' contains 'not mentioned' and scores 1.0 (firm refusal), despite providing a hallucinated answer. This is a partial-abstention-then-hallucination pattern that should score lower (e.g., 0.3-0.5) rather than getting full credit.

Phrases most susceptible to false positives in non-refusal contexts:
- 'not mentioned' / 'not specified' / 'not available' — can appear in hedging before answering
- 'not found' — can appear as 'the information was not found to directly state...'
- 'not documented' — 'while not documented explicitly, it appears to be...'

The current scorer rewards any response that includes a refusal phrase, even if the response then proceeds to hallucinate an answer. A more robust scorer would check whether the response primarily abstains vs primarily answers.
close_reason: NOT A BUG: NegativeTask scoring uses a tiered priority system with early returns (negative.py:143-166). Firm refusal phrases return 1.0 immediately by design — the abstention intent is prioritized. This is a deliberate design choice, not a bug.

title: CompositeVariant concatenates full independent renders, inflating prompt 10x
description:
File: agent-evals/src/agent_evals/variants/composite.py

CompositeVariant.render() calls each component's render(doc_tree) independently, then concatenates with '\n\n'. Since every axis (1-10) produces a COMPLETE rendering of the doc_tree, a 10-axis Taguchi composite produces 10 separate renderings of the same documentation (e.g., a flat list + YAML output + pipe-delimited table + noise-augmented list + section-level entries + ...).

This means:
1. The prompt is ~10x longer than any single variant, consuming excessive tokens
2. The LLM sees the same documentation repeated 10 different ways — unlike any real documentation format
3. Taguchi S/N ratios measure the combined effect of 10 concatenated renderings, not isolated axis effects
4. The additivity assumption (axes are independent) is violated since each axis's contribution depends on how much context the other 9 renderings consume

Expected behavior: A composite should produce ONE rendering that combines properties from each axis (e.g., YAML format + section granularity + noise injection + BLUF ordering), not 10 independent renderings concatenated together.

Fix: Refactor CompositeVariant to use a pipeline/decorator pattern where axes modify a single base rendering rather than each producing an independent one. For example: scale selects files → structure organizes them → format renders → noise adds distractors → position reorders → metadata enriches.
close_reason: Fixed and verified: all 3460 tests pass

title: Bug: LLM judge uses evaluation model instead of JUDGE_MODEL
description:
Two issues in runner.py:799-806 (_call_judge method):

1. Judge model not passed to LLM call: Code retrieves self._config.judge_model but calls self._client.complete(messages) WITHOUT passing model= kwarg. The complete() method uses self.model (the evaluation model) when no model= kwarg is provided. Fix: change line 806 to self._client.complete(messages, model=judge_model).content

2. No --judge-model CLI flag: There is no CLI flag to configure the judge model. Only --judge-mode and --judge-sample-rate exist. The judge model should be selectable via --judge-model CLI flag (defaulting to openrouter/openai/gpt-4o-mini) and configurable in YAML.
close_reason: Fixed and verified: all 3460 tests pass

title: Bug: Pipeline confirmation phase loses prediction interval from screening
description: In pipeline.py run_confirmation() (lines 219-222), the OptimalPrediction is reconstructed with only optimal_assignment and predicted_sn. The prediction_interval and se_prediction computed during screening are NOT carried forward. validate_confirmation() then falls back to hardcoded +/-1.0 dB interval and se=1.0, making confirmation validation meaningless. Fix: store prediction_interval and se_prediction in PhaseResult during screening and pass them to the reconstructed OptimalPrediction.
close_reason: FIXED: Prediction interval IS preserved. Confirmation phase correctly receives screening_result.optimal and screening_result.predicted_sn (pipeline.py:240-243), passes to validate_confirmation() which uses the interval (analysis.py:534-538).

title: Bug: Retrieval fuzzy match inflates scores - same path matches multiple expected
description: In retrieval.py lines 110-115, the fuzzy basename matching loop breaks after matching an extracted path to one expected path, but does NOT remove the extracted path from unmatched_extracted. The same extracted file can match multiple expected files. Example: expected=[src/auth.py, lib/auth.py], extracted=[vendor/auth.py] gives fuzzy_hits=1.0 when only 0.5 is deserved. This can make precision and recall exceed 1.0 before clamping. Fix: remove matched extracted paths from unmatched_extracted after each basename match.
close_reason: Fixed and verified: all 3460 tests pass

title: Bug: RobustnessTask missing fuzzy matching despite docstring claim
description: robustness.py docstring says 'Reuses the same scoring logic as FactExtractionTask' but only implements exact/alias/keyword fallback. FactExtractionTask has a 4-layer cascade: exact -> alias -> fuzzy@85 (0.9) -> fuzzy@70 (0.7) -> keyword. RobustnessTask skips the rapidfuzz layers entirely. This is especially problematic because robustness tasks test perturbed inputs (typos, paraphrases) where fuzzy matching matters most. A response scoring 0.9 in FactExtraction could score much lower in Robustness due to the missing fuzzy layer.

title: Phase C: Premium loading skeleton
Bug: Pipeline refinement phase never analyzes its trial results
description: In pipeline.py run_refinement() (lines 274-281), the PhaseResult is returned with only raw trials - no main_effects, anova, optimal, or significant_factors are computed. The final_optimal on line 392 always falls back to screening.optimal because refinement.optimal is always None. This means the refinement phase (full factorial on top-K factors) runs expensive trials but never identifies whether a different combination is better than the screening prediction. Fix: add analysis computation to run_refinement() similar to run_screening().
close_reason: Fixed and verified: all 3460 tests pass

title: Bug: Silent rate-limit retry uses deterministic backoff (thundering herd)
description: PARTIALLY FIXED: The retryable exception path (client.py:186-192) correctly uses random.uniform(0, max_delay) for jitter. However, the silent rate-limit retry path (client.py:151-159) for content=None responses still uses deterministic exponential backoff: delay = RETRY_BASE_DELAY * (2 ** attempt) with no jitter. When multiple threads hit rate limits simultaneously, they all retry at the exact same time. Fix: change line 153 to use random.uniform(0, delay) like the exception path.
close_reason: Fixed: silent rate-limit retry now uses random.uniform(0, max_delay) jitter

title: Bug: TaguchiRunner silently swallows all exceptions as failed trials
description: In taguchi/runner.py line 337, _run_trial() catches all Exception types and returns an error TrialResult with score=0.0. Programming bugs (TypeError, AttributeError, KeyError) are silently recorded as 'failed trials' instead of propagating. Compare with EvalRunner._run_trial() which lets exceptions propagate to the caller. This makes debugging very difficult - a bug in task.build_prompt() or task.score_response() appears as a low score rather than a crash. Fix: only catch expected exceptions (LLM errors, network errors) or re-raise non-retriable errors.

title: Bug: Report aggregator uses z=1.96 for confidence intervals regardless of sample size
description: In reports/aggregator.py lines 65-68, confidence intervals use z=1.96 (normal approximation) even for small samples (2-30 trials). For n=2, the correct t-distribution multiplier is ~12.7, not 1.96. This makes confidence intervals far too narrow for small samples, potentially leading to false conclusions about variant differences. Fix: use scipy.stats.t.ppf(0.975, df=count-1) instead of the hardcoded 1.96 multiplier.

title: Bug: Retrieval file path regex only matches 8 extensions
description: In retrieval.py lines 19-22, _FILE_PATH_PATTERN only matches: md|py|yaml|yml|json|toml|txt|rst|html. Missing common extensions: .ts, .tsx, .js, .jsx, .css, .scss, .go, .rs, .java, .xml, .cfg, .ini, .sh, .bash, .dockerfile, .env, .rb, .php, .c, .cpp, .h. Any retrieval task with expected files using these extensions will fail to extract them from responses, yielding score=0.0. Fix: expand the extension list or use a more permissive pattern like [\w.-]+\.\w{1,10}.

title: Bug: CompositeVariant.teardown() skips remaining components on exception
description: In variants/composite.py lines 87-90, teardown() iterates components without try/except per component. If any component's teardown() raises, remaining components are never torn down. Same issue exists in setup() (lines 82-85) - no rollback of already-setup components on partial failure. Compare with EvalRunner.run() (runner.py:385-393) and TaguchiRunner (taguchi/runner.py:240-247) which wrap individual teardowns. Fix: wrap each component teardown in try/except; add setup rollback logic.

title: Context delivery sends index-only, not doc content — all knowledge tasks affected
description: The Taguchi screening prompts contain a doc INDEX (file paths, summaries, token counts) but NOT the actual document content. The model is asked to answer questions about documents it can only see titles of. This makes all knowledge-dependent task types (fact_extraction, multi_hop, disambiguation, conflicting, retrieval) measure 'how much info leaks through summaries' rather than 'which index format works best'. The context strategy or variant rendering needs to include actual doc content, not just the index listing.

title: CodeRAGBench adapter expected_files paths don't match doc tree — retrieval always 0.0
description: CodeRAGBenchAdapter.convert_tasks() generates expected_files like 'library-docs/has_close_elements.md' from HumanEval docs field, but build_doc_tree() loads library-documentation corpus with paths like 'library-docs/tensorflow/aggregationmethod.md'. These are entirely disjoint path spaces. The retrieval task scores 0.0 structurally because expected files can never exist in the index. Fix: either include HumanEval docs in the corpus, or map queries to actual library-documentation entries.

title: DS1000 adapter stores reference_code as test field — scorer regex mismatch caps score at 0.3
description: ds1000.py stores reference_code (executable Python wrapper function) in metadata.test, but CodeGenerationTask scorer treats test lines as regex patterns. Brackets in code like df.iloc[List] are interpreted as regex character classes, causing 0/N pattern matches always. Max score = 0.3 (syntax + no-violations only). Fix: either store actual test assertions, use execution-based scoring, or escape regex metacharacters in the scorer.

title: Phase E: Copy button morph
SWE-bench adapter task metadata points to wrong files and generic summaries
description: swe_bench.py generates agentic tasks where the files metadata points to docs/README.md with summary 'Repository documentation for org/repo' instead of actual code files relevant to the bug. The scorer checks for exact file paths and test names from metadata, so scores are near 0 even when the model gives intelligent responses. Fix: populate files with actual relevant source files and meaningful summaries from the SWE-bench instance data.

title: extract_keywords() doesn't strip quotes causing false negatives in conflicting scoring
WikiContradict expected_resolution is boilerplate template, should use ref_answer
Disambiguation tasks score 1.0 with zero variance (trivially answerable)
Retrieval task prompt needs strengthening to prevent code-only responses
Judge model not wired through despite CLI flag
description: Judge model IS wired in full mode but NOT in taguchi mode. TaguchiRunner._run_trial has independent implementation that never checks judge_enabled. Dead constants JUDGE_SAMPLE_RATE=50 and JUDGE_MODEL in runner.py. Fix: port judge sampling block from EvalRunner._run_trial to TaguchiRunner._run_trial.

title: BigCodeBench expected_answers are boilerplate — CompositionalTask keyword scoring inflated
description: BigCodeBench adapter (bigcodebench.py lines 66-73) generates expected_answers as 'Use {lib} API as shown in the solution.' for every sub-question. These boilerplate strings cause CompositionalTask._score_sub_answer() to match on generic keywords like 'pandas', 'API', 'shown', 'solution' rather than testing whether the LLM produced the actual canonical_solution logic. Any response mentioning library names scores high, compressing Taguchi S/N variance. Fix: extract meaningful patterns from canonical_solution per library (similar to DS1000's _extract_key_patterns approach).

title: MultiHop-RAG adapter emits tasks with empty reasoning_chain — scorer returns 1.0 unconditionally
description: MultiHop-RAG adapter (multihop_rag.py lines 56-62) constructs reasoning_chain and question_decomposition from evidence_list entries. When evidence_list is empty or missing (record.get('evidence_list') returns [] or None), both lists are empty. MultiHopTask.score_response() returns 1.0 when steps is empty (line 98: 'if not steps: return 1.0'). These vacuous-1.0 tasks inflate mean scores and collapse variance, distorting Taguchi factor effect estimates. Fix: skip records with empty evidence_list in convert_tasks() (add a 'if not evidence: continue' guard, similar to CodeRAGBench's 'if not docs: continue').

title: CompositeVariant silently discards 9/10 axes: no variants implement PRE_RENDER or POST_RENDER pipeline roles

comments.author: Trevor Leigh
comments.text: The CompositeVariant pipeline fix (bead #135) introduced PRE_RENDER/PRIMARY/POST_RENDER roles, but NO real variant implements PRE_RENDER or POST_RENDER. All 47+ variants default to PipelineRole.PRIMARY. When a Taguchi OA row combines variants from axes 1-10, _select_primary() picks only the lowest-axis variant (axis 1 = structure). Axes 2-10 are silently discarded. This means Taguchi screening results are meaningless for 9 out of 10 factors.

title: AmbigQA singleAnswer records emitted as disambiguation tasks with 1 interpretation — trivially 1.0
description: AmbigQA adapter (ambigqa.py lines 74-82) falls back to singleAnswer records when no multipleQAs annotations exist. These records have only 1 interpretation (interpretation_0). DisambiguationTask scorer awards coverage=1/1=1.0 and correctness~1.0 trivially, producing uninformative scores. These records are not genuinely ambiguous and should be filtered out. Fix: add a guard 'if len(interpretations) < 2: continue' after building interpretations (before line 84), or map singleAnswer records to fact_extraction instead.

title: Phase E: Sort column flip
MultiHop-RAG build_doc_tree model_copy skips size_bytes/token_count update — total_tokens undercount
description: MultiHop-RAG adapter (multihop_rag.py lines 108-113) appends content to existing DocFile via model_copy(update={'content': ...}) but does not update size_bytes or token_count. For multi-fact documents (same source cited in multiple evidence entries), size_bytes and token_count retain values from the first fact only. The DocTree.total_tokens sum (line 129) therefore undercounts actual tokens. This affects context delivery strategies that use token_count for budget allocation, potentially truncating documents or making suboptimal selections. Fix: include size_bytes and token_count in the model_copy update dict, recalculating from the new content.

title: BigCodeBench adapter emits tasks with empty libs — CompositionalTask scores vacuous 1.0
description: BigCodeBench adapter (bigcodebench.py lines 58-62, 66-73) does not filter out records where libs is empty. When libs=[], both sub_questions and expected_answers are empty lists. CompositionalTask.score_response() returns 1.0 when self.sub_tasks is empty (line 106: 'if not self.sub_tasks: return 1.0'). These vacuous-1.0 tasks inflate mean scores and collapse variance in Taguchi screening. Fix: add 'if not libs: continue' guard before task generation (after line 62).

title: CompositeVariant.metadata() token_estimate is sum of all axes but only one axis renders

comments.author: Trevor Leigh
comments.text: CompositeVariant.metadata().token_estimate sums all component estimates (line 91), but render() only uses one PRIMARY component. The reported estimate is 5-10x higher than the actual rendered output. This inflates dry-run cost estimates and may mislead token budget decisions. Fix: sum should only include the primary component plus any PRE/POST overhead.

title: SystemPromptStrategy priority_truncate assembles raw doc content instead of rendered index lines

comments.author: Trevor Leigh
comments.text: In SystemPromptStrategy._priority_truncate() (system_prompt.py:125-173), when the rendered index exceeds the token budget, the method sorts by doc_tree tier using sort_files_bluf(), then assembles output by concatenating doc_file.content (raw document content) rather than re-rendering the truncated index. This means: (1) The strategy returns raw doc content instead of the variant's rendered format, defeating the purpose of testing index FORMAT effects. (2) The returned text bears no relation to the rendered_index that was passed in. (3) The truncation discards the variant's rendering entirely. Fix: The priority truncation should operate on the rendered_index string, not bypass it with raw doc content.

title: ANOVA uses inconsistent row sets: grand_mean excludes all-dummy rows but per-factor SS includes partial-dummy rows
description: In run_anova() (analysis.py:232-264), grand_mean is computed from non_dummy_rows (rows with NO dummy factors), but each factor's SS computation iterates ALL design.rows, only skipping rows where THAT factor has a dummy. A row with a dummy in axis_3 is excluded from grand_mean but included in SS for axis_1 and axis_2. This breaks the ANOVA identity (SS_total \!= sum(SS_factor) + SS_error) and produces incorrect F-ratios, p-values, and effect sizes in mixed-level designs. Fix: use the same row set for grand_mean and per-factor level_groups -- either exclude all partial-dummy rows globally, or use per-factor grand means.

title: DS1000 _extract_key_patterns returns empty for top-level assignment solutions — vacuous 1.0 scores
description: DS1000 adapter's _extract_key_patterns (ds1000.py lines 29-75) only extracts patterns from FunctionDef return values/expressions via AST. Many DS-1000 solutions are top-level assignments like 'result = df.groupby(A).sum()' without function wrappers. For these: (1) AST finds no FunctionDef -> patterns=[], (2) heuristic fallback skips lines starting with 'result ' (line 83: skip_prefixes includes 'result '). Result: test_field is empty string. CodeGenerationTask scorer treats empty patterns as vacuously satisfied (match_rate=1.0), yielding score ~1.0 for any response. Fix: (a) extend AST extraction to handle top-level assignments/expressions, OR (b) in heuristic, extract RHS of 'result = ...' assignments instead of skipping them entirely.

title: predict_optimal grand_mean averages all level means, biasing mixed-level designs
description: In predict_optimal() (analysis.py:508-511), grand_mean is computed as the simple average of ALL level means across ALL factors. With mixed-level designs (e.g., factor A has 5 levels, factor B has 2), factor A contributes 5 values and factor B contributes 2, weighting A higher. The correct grand mean should be the mean of all S/N observations (available via sn_ratios param) or the mean of per-factor means. The same bug exists in _compute_additivity_r_squared() (analysis.py:589-590). This causes incorrect optimal S/N predictions and potentially misleading additivity R-squared values. For symmetric OAs the error is zero; for mixed-level designs (L18, L36, L50) it biases the predicted S/N.

title: Noise variants produce duplicate distractor paths across different noise levels (same seed=42)

comments.author: Trevor Leigh
comments.text: All noise variants (noise_25, noise_50, noise_75) use random.Random(42) as the seed and generate_distractors() produces paths like docs/internal/generated_001.md, generated_002.md, etc. Since the path pattern is index-based (not random), noise-25 generates generated_001..007, noise-50 generates generated_001..020, and noise-75 generates generated_001..060. The first N distractors are IDENTICAL across noise levels. In a Taguchi screening comparing noise levels, the shared distractors reduce the measured difference between levels, biasing effect sizes toward zero. Fix: Use a different seed per noise level or include the noise percentage in the distractor path pattern.

title: RAG strategy builds duplicate embeddings of task question for each trial (no caching)

comments.author: Trevor Leigh
comments.text: In RAGStrategy.prepare(), self._embedder.embed(question) is called for every trial (task x repetition x OA row). Since many tasks repeat the same question across repetitions, the same embedding is computed redundantly. For a Taguchi run with 50 OA rows x 355 tasks x 3 reps, that's 53,250 embedding API calls when many could be cached. Fix: Add an LRU cache on question text or embed all unique questions upfront during setup.

title: Confirmation phase still loses prediction interval from screening (bead #137 falsely closed)
description: Bead #137 was closed as 'FIXED' but the bug persists. In pipeline.py:393-396, OptimalPrediction is reconstructed with only optimal_assignment and predicted_sn -- prediction_interval and se_prediction are NOT passed. validate_confirmation() (analysis.py:652-656) falls back to hardcoded +/-1.0 interval and se=1.0, making confirmation validation statistically meaningless. PhaseResult does not store prediction_interval or se_prediction from screening, so they are lost between phases. Fix: store the screening OptimalPrediction's interval/SE in PhaseResult and pass them to the reconstructed OptimalPrediction in run_confirmation().

title: Phase E: Button press ripple
xref_dense and xref_light stem matching produces false positives for short stems (e.g. 'api' matches 'api_key')

comments.author: Trevor Leigh
comments.text: In xref_dense.py line 78, the stem matching uses 'stem.lower() in content_lower' which is a substring match, not a word boundary match. A file named 'api.md' has stem 'api', which will match any content containing 'api' as a substring (e.g. 'api_key', 'capital', 'rapid'). This inflates cross-reference counts and adds noise to the xref-dense variant output. The metadata_with_related.py variant correctly uses re.compile(rf'\b{re.escape(target_stem)}\b') for word-boundary matching. Fix: Use word-boundary regex instead of 'in' substring check, consistent with metadata_with_related.py.

title: _select_client crashes with KeyError when model factor gets DUMMY_LEVEL in mixed-level OA
description: In TaguchiRunner._select_client() (runner.py:476-481), when 'model' is a Taguchi factor and the OA assigns a dummy level (row.assignments['model'] == '__dummy__'), the code does self._clients['__dummy__'] which raises KeyError. _build_composite() correctly skips DUMMY_LEVEL for axis factors (line 471-472), but _select_client() has no such check. This crashes multi-model Taguchi runs when using mixed-level OAs (L18, L36, L50, etc.) where the model column has more OA levels than actual models. Fix: check for DUMMY_LEVEL in _select_client and fall back to the default client.

title: WikiContradict adapter does not filter empty ref_answer — ConflictingTask scores constant 0.0
description: WikiContradict adapter (wikicontradict.py lines 55-104) does not filter out records where ref_answer is empty. When ref_answer='', the task's expected_resolution is empty string. ConflictingTask.score_response() returns 0.0 immediately when expected_resolution is empty (line 73: 'if not self.expected_resolution: return 0.0'). These constant-0.0 tasks compress variance just as badly as vacuous-1.0 tasks, distorting Taguchi factor S/N ratio estimates. Fix: add 'if not record.get("ref_answer"): continue' guard to skip records without gold answers.

title: FullContextStrategy appends same doc content regardless of variant, diluting axis effects in Taguchi screening

comments.author: Trevor Leigh
comments.text: FullContextStrategy._build_full_content() (full.py:47-71) appends the full raw content of every doc file after the rendered index. The appended content is identical regardless of which variant rendered the index. For a sample fixture with 20 files / 4127 tokens, the raw doc content may be 10-50x larger than the rendered index. This means the LLM prompt is dominated by the SAME raw content across all variant conditions, and the varying rendered index is a small prefix. Effect: Taguchi S/N ratios are dominated by the constant doc content, washing out differences between index format variants. The measured axis effects will be attenuated toward zero. Fix: Either (1) make FullContextStrategy respect the variant's choices (e.g. scale variants should also limit which files' content is appended), or (2) document that full_context strategy is expected to show smaller axis effects.

title: Pipeline screening includes axis 0 baselines as Taguchi factors unlike standalone mode
description: In DOEPipeline.run_screening() (pipeline.py:240-265), axis 0 baseline variants are included in the axes dict passed to build_design(). The usable_axes validation (line 248) filters out axis 0 for the >= 2 check, but the full axes dict (including axis 0) is passed to build_design (line 264). This wastes an OA column on baselines and includes them as an experimental factor in the ANOVA, distorting factor significance results. In contrast, _run_taguchi() in cli.py (lines 1023-1024) correctly excludes axis 0 with 'if m.axis == 0: continue'. Fix: filter axis 0 out of axes dict before passing to build_design in run_screening(), matching the standalone Taguchi mode behavior.

title: TaguchiRunner._build_composite crashes if all factors in an OA row are dummy level

comments.author: Trevor Leigh
comments.text: In taguchi/runner.py:463-474, _build_composite() skips dummy-level assignments and builds a components dict. If all factors in an OA row happen to be dummy level, the dict is empty and CompositeVariant({}) raises ValueError. While unlikely with current OA designs, it's possible with mixed-level arrays where multiple factors have fewer levels than the OA column width. Fix: Either skip the entire row (exclude from trials) or return a minimal fallback composite.

title: ToolBasedStrategy.execute() turns zero total cost into None via 'sum(...) or None'

comments.author: Trevor Leigh
comments.text: In tool_based.py:187, total_cost is computed as 'sum(g.cost for g in generations if g.cost is not None) or None'. The 'or None' is intended to handle the case where no generations have a cost. But 'sum(...)' returns 0.0 when all costs are zero (free models), and 0.0 is falsy in Python, so total_cost becomes None. This means: (1) Free model runs report cost=None instead of cost=0.0 (2) Cost tracking loses data for free-tier models. Fix: Use a conditional expression instead: 'costs = [g.cost for g in generations if g.cost is not None]; total_cost = sum(costs) if costs else None'.

comments.author: Trevor Leigh
comments.text: Same pattern exists in mcp_native.py:221 and dynamic_tools.py:208. All three multi-turn strategies have the same zero-cost-becomes-None bug.

title: Strategy registry returns singleton, TaguchiRunner shares one strategy across all OA rows
description: The context strategy registry (context/registry.py:22) creates singleton instances per class. get_strategy_by_name() returns this singleton. The orchestrator's _build_strategy_factory() (orchestrator.py:457-466) calls get_strategy_by_name() which returns the same instance every time. In TaguchiRunner.run() (runner.py:124-133), the loop 'strategy = self._strategy_factory()' for each OA row gets the SAME singleton. Each row calls strategy.setup(rendered, doc_tree) which overwrites the previous row's state. All entries in row_strategies point to the SAME object, so only the LAST row's setup survives. For RAGStrategy (rag.py:44-59), this means all rows use the last row's embeddings. For ToolBasedStrategy (tool_based.py:99-101), all rows use the last row's rendered_index. This silently corrupts results for RAG and tool-based strategies in Taguchi mode. Fix: factory must create NEW instances, not return the singleton.

title: Error trials (score=0.0) included in S/N and ANOVA, biasing screening results
description: When _run_trial() catches an exception (runner.py:407-434), it returns score=0.0 with error set. In pipeline.run_screening() (pipeline.py:284-287), ALL trial scores are grouped by OA row without filtering out error trials. These 0.0 scores from API failures, timeouts, or rate limits are included in compute_sn_ratios() and run_anova(), biasing S/N ratios downward and inflating error variance. Under higher concurrency or flaky API conditions, this can produce unreliable factor significance rankings. Fix: filter out trials where trial.error is not None before grouping scores for S/N computation.

title: compute_main_effects returns 0.0 for unobserved levels, biasing optimal prediction
description: In compute_main_effects() (analysis.py:202-207), when a factor level has zero observations (all rows with that level were excluded as dummies), the code returns 0.0 as the mean S/N. Since S/N ratios are typically in the range [0, 40] dB for larger-is-better, a 0.0 mean makes that level appear catastrophically bad. predict_optimal() then never selects that level, even though no data exists to judge it. Also, the 0.0 is included in the grand_mean computation (analysis.py:508-511), pulling it downward. Fix: use NaN or exclude unobserved levels from main_effects entirely; downstream consumers (predict_optimal, ANOVA) should skip NaN levels.

Substring containment matching in 6 scorers gives false 1.0 for short expected answers
description:
Files: agent-evals/src/agent_evals/tasks/fact_extraction.py, robustness.py, efficiency.py, conflicting.py, compositional.py (exact containment layer)

Six scorers use bare 'expected_lower in response_lower' substring containment as their first scoring layer. This causes false-positive 1.0 scores when the expected answer is a short string that appears as a substring of unrelated words in the response.

Demonstrated false positives:
- '300' in '3000' -> 1.0 (wrong number matches)
- 'run' in 'running'/'runtime' -> 1.0
- 'no' in 'know'/'not'/'noticed' -> 1.0 (conflicting_001 example)
- 'id' in 'said'/'considered' -> 1.0
- 'go' in 'going'/'google' -> 1.0
- '10' in '100'/'1000' -> 1.0
- '5' in '50'/'15'/'25' -> 1.0

The gold standard contains many short expected_answers: '300', '5', '6', '10', '20', '100', 'run', 'admin', 'INFO', 'HS256', etc. All of these are susceptible.

Impact on Taguchi: inflated scores reduce variance between factor levels, masking real effects. Short answers dominate easy/medium difficulty tasks which are the bulk of the task pool.

Fix: use word-boundary regex (\b) for expected answers <= 5 characters, or always for numeric answers. The multi_hop scorer already does this correctly for short keywords (see _keyword_in_response).

title: Negative scorer produces only 4 discrete values {0.0, 0.3, 0.7, 1.0} — poor Taguchi discrimination
description:
File: agent-evals/src/agent_evals/tasks/negative.py

The NegativeTask scorer uses a tiered phrase-matching rubric that can only produce exactly 4 scores: 1.0 (firm refusal), 0.7 (hedge), 0.3 (disclaimer), 0.0 (hallucination). In practice, the ANSWER_WITH_DISCLAIMER phrases are extremely specific and rarely produced by modern LLMs ('based on limited information', 'this may not be accurate', 'i'm making an assumption'), so the effective output is {0.0, 0.7, 1.0} — only 3 distinct values.

This is the most coarse-grained scorer among all 11 task types. For Taguchi screening, low-variance scoring reduces the signal-to-noise ratio, making it harder to detect factor effects. When negative tasks are sampled into an OA row, their scores contribute essentially no discriminating information between factor levels.

Possible improvements:
1. Add more tiers (e.g., 0.5 for partial hedging, 0.85 for strong hedge)
2. Scale by response length — shorter refusals are better
3. Penalize refusal-then-hallucination pattern (currently scores 1.0 per closed bead #134's design decision, but a 0.8 for 'refusal + answer' vs 1.0 for 'pure refusal' would add granularity)
4. Score confidence language on a continuous scale using keyword density

title: Compositional scorer partial_ratio inflates scores for short keywords against longer strings
description:
File: agent-evals/src/agent_evals/tasks/compositional.py

The _score_sub_answer() method falls back to rapidfuzz partial_ratio with cutoff=80 for keyword matching. partial_ratio matches the shorter string as a substring window within the longer string, which causes inflated scores when keywords are short numbers or common words.

Demonstrated false positives:
- partial_ratio('300', '3000 items') = 100.0  (wrong number)
- partial_ratio('pipeline.run', 'pipelines running fast') = 91.7  (unrelated context)
- partial_ratio('v2.2.0', 'version 2.2.0') = 90.9  (acceptable)

The first two are problematic: a response mentioning '3000' gets full keyword credit for expected answer '300', and a response about 'pipelines running' gets credit for 'pipeline.run()'.

Impact: compositional tasks with short expected sub-answers will have inflated scores, reducing between-level variance in Taguchi screening.

Fix: use token_sort_ratio or token_set_ratio instead of partial_ratio, or add a length check that requires word-boundary matching for keywords <= 4 characters. Alternatively, raise the cutoff to 90+ for short keywords.

title: Retrieval scorer file-path regex matches version numbers like v2.2.0 as false file paths
description:
File: agent-evals/src/agent_evals/tasks/retrieval.py

The _FILE_PATH_PATTERN regex (r'(?:[\w./-]+/)?[\w.-]+\.\w{1,10}') matches version numbers like 'v2.2.0' as file paths because the pattern accepts dot-separated segments with a 1-10 character 'extension'. When an LLM response mentions version numbers alongside actual file paths, these false matches inflate the extracted file set, reducing precision in the F-beta calculation.

Demonstrated:
- Input: 'api/caching.md\nconfig/settings.py\nv2.2.0'
- Expected F-beta: 1.0 (both files present)
- Actual F-beta: 0.909 (precision drops from 2/3 extracted being real files)

Other false matches: URLs (https://example.com/path.html extracts as //example.com/path.html), IP addresses with ports (192.168.1.50), floats in prose (3.14).

Impact: minor (~0.09 point reduction per false positive), but systematic across responses that discuss versioned software.

Fix: require at least one '/' directory separator for paths, or add a negative lookbehind for 'v' followed by digits-and-dots to exclude version patterns.

title: Code generation scorer gives 0.9-1.0 for any response when test field is empty (vacuously satisfied)
description:
File: agent-evals/src/agent_evals/tasks/code_generation.py

When the test field is empty or missing, the scorer sets match_rate = 1.0 (vacuously satisfied). Combined with the 0.2 no-violation bonus and 0.1 syntax bonus, any response scores at least 0.9 (invalid Python) or 1.0 (valid Python or no code), regardless of correctness.

The existing gold standard tasks all have non-empty test fields so this primarily affects external HF datasets. Bead #185 covers the DS1000 case specifically (empty patterns from _extract_key_patterns), but this is the general scorer-side issue: the scorer should not treat empty test as vacuously correct.

Demonstrated:
- 'I have no idea what you want' scores 0.90 with empty test
- 'def goodbye(): pass' (wrong code) scores 1.00 with empty test

Fix: when test is empty AND expected_answer is non-empty, fall back to keyword matching against expected_answer. When both are empty, return 0.5 (unknown) rather than 1.0 (perfect).

title: Pipeline resume loses predicted_sn: not stored in phase_results DB, reconstructed screening has None
description: When a pipeline resumes after screening is complete (pipeline.py:551-566), the PhaseResult is reconstructed from the DB via get_phase_results(). However, predicted_sn is NOT stored in save_phase_results() (store.py:598-635) and NOT returned by get_phase_results() (store.py:658-668). The reconstructed screening PhaseResult has predicted_sn=None (dataclass default). In run_confirmation (pipeline.py:395), 'screening_result.predicted_sn or 0.0' evaluates to 0.0, making the confirmation validation compare against predicted S/N of 0.0. Bead #87 fixed the non-resume path but the resume path still has this defect. Fix: add predicted_sn to the phase_results table schema, save it in save_phase_results, return it in get_phase_results, and set it in the resume reconstruction.

title: Bug: disambiguation _AMBIGUITY_PHRASES contains overly broad 'interpret' causing false positive awareness scores
description: File: agent-evals/src/agent_evals/tasks/disambiguation.py, line 29. The _AMBIGUITY_PHRASES tuple includes the bare word 'interpret' which is far too common in LLM responses. Phrases like 'I interpret the question as...' or 'The correct interpretation is...' trigger the awareness axis (20% weight) even though they don't genuinely acknowledge ambiguity. All other phrases in the tuple are multi-word and specific (e.g. 'multiple interpretations', 'could mean'). Fix: Remove 'interpret' or replace with more specific phrases like 'multiple interpretations' (already present) or 'can be interpreted'.

title: Bug: aggregate_turn_metrics converts unknown cost (all None) to 0 instead of None
description: File: agent-evals/src/agent_evals/metrics/operational.py, line 100. In aggregate_turn_metrics(), the expression sum(t.cost_usd for t in turns if t.cost_usd) has two problems: (1) When all turns have cost_usd=None, the generator is empty and sum() returns 0 (int), making total_cost_usd=0. This loses the 'unknown cost' semantic that None represents. (2) The filter 'if t.cost_usd' also excludes cost_usd=0.0 (free models), though this doesn't affect the sum. Fix: Use None when all costs are None, and filter with 'is not None' instead of truthiness.

title: Bug: loader duplicate ID check misaligns tasks with file paths when schema.yaml is skipped
description: File: agent-evals/src/agent_evals/tasks/loader.py, lines 152-162. The duplicate ID check builds loaded_paths by filtering yaml_paths against error paths, but yaml_paths includes schema.yaml which is skipped via 'continue' (not via an error). So schema.yaml appears in loaded_paths despite having no task in the tasks list. zip(tasks, loaded_paths) then misaligns, pairing tasks with wrong file paths. Example: yaml_paths=[a.yaml, schema.yaml, b.yaml], tasks=[task_a, task_b] -> zip pairs task_b with schema.yaml. Fix: Track successful paths alongside tasks, or also exclude skipped files from loaded_paths.

title: Bug: CompositionalTask zip(questions, answers) silently truncates mismatched parallel lists
description: File: agent-evals/src/agent_evals/tasks/compositional.py, lines 42-45. When using the parallel-list format (sub_questions + expected_answers), zip(questions, answers) silently truncates to the shorter list if they have different lengths. This silently drops sub-questions without answers or answers without questions. Fix: Use zip(questions, answers, strict=True) to raise ValueError on length mismatch, or at minimum log a warning.

description: File: agent-evals/src/agent_evals/judge/hallucination.py, line 98. parse_hallucination_result() passes the LLM-generated hallucination_score directly to HallucinationResult without clamping to [0.0, 1.0]. title: Bug: CodeGenerationTask concatenates multi-language code blocks before syntax check, causing false penalty
description: File: agent-evals/src/agent_evals/tasks/code_generation.py, lines 188-191. _extract_code_blocks() concatenates ALL fenced code blocks into one string, but _detect_language() only reads the language tag from the FIRST block. When a response has blocks in multiple languages (e.g. Python + JavaScript), the concatenated code is parsed as Python (first block's language), causing a SyntaxError penalty even though each individual block is valid. Fix: Either check syntax per-block with each block's own language tag, or only validate the first block.

title: Bug: NavigationPathMetric _READ_TOOL_PATTERN falsely matches write/delete/create tools as file reads
description: File: agent-evals/src/agent_evals/metrics/navigation.py, lines 15-17. The _READ_TOOL_PATTERN regex r'read|open|file|get' matches 'file' which causes write_file, delete_file, create_file, and other non-read file operations to be counted as file reads. This inflates total_reads, which: (1) reduces the efficiency sub-score (optimal/actual), (2) reduces the relevance sub-score if write paths don't match relevant files, and (3) increases the backtracking penalty if the same file is written then read. Fix: Use a more specific pattern like r'read_file|read|open_file|get_file' or exclude known write/delete patterns.

title: Bug: Retrieval _FILE_PATH_PATTERN matches version numbers and decimals as file paths (false positives)
description: File: agent-evals/src/agent_evals/tasks/retrieval.py, lines 21-24. The permissive regex r'(?:[\w./-]+/)?[\w.-]+\.\w{1,10}' (introduced to fix #144) now matches non-file strings like version numbers ('3.11', 'v2.0'), decimal numbers ('3.14'), and abbreviation fragments ('e.g' from 'e.g.'). These false positives inflate extracted_norm, increasing the precision denominator and lowering the F-beta score. Fix: Require either a directory prefix (/) or a minimum of 2 chars before the dot, and/or add a negative lookbehind for common false positive patterns.

L36 OA construction produces duplicate columns — factors assigned to aliased columns are completely confounded
description:
## Bug
`_build_l36()` in `agent-evals/src/agent_evals/taguchi/catalog.py:204` constructs the L36 OA using a Kronecker product of L4×L9 with column duplication. The resulting 23-column matrix has only 7 distinct columns: 3 unique 2-level columns (each repeated 3-4 times) and 4 unique 3-level columns (each repeated 3 times).

## Evidence
Verified numerically: 26 pairs of IDENTICAL columns found:
- 2-level: cols 0=3=6=9, cols 1=4=7=10, cols 2=5=8
- 3-level: cols 11=13=19, cols 12=14=20, cols 15=17=21, cols 16=18=22

## Impact
If two factors are assigned to duplicate columns (e.g., cols 0 and 3), their Taguchi main effects are IDENTICAL and completely confounded. The ANOVA will attribute the same variance to both factors, making screening results meaningless. With 4+ two-level factors, `build_design` assigns them to cols 0,1,2,3 — and cols 0 and 3 are identical.

## Fix
Replace the naive Kronecker construction with the published L36 table from Taguchi & Konishi (1987). The standard L36(2^11×3^12) has 23 independent columns. Alternatively, use a verified programmatic construction.

## Test gap
`test_taguchi_catalog.py` only tests pairwise balance for L4, L9, L121, L169 — NOT for L36, L50, or L54.

title: L50 OA construction produces confounded column pairs — 3 pairs within 10-factor assignment range are non-orthogonal
description:
## Bug
`_build_l50()` in `agent-evals/src/agent_evals/taguchi/catalog.py:243` constructs the L50 OA using a shifted-column pattern: columns 7-11 are `(base_col + a) % 5` where `a` is the 2-level column 0. This creates 5 confounded column pairs: {1,7}, {2,8}, {3,9}, {4,10}, {5,11}. For each pair, only 10 of 25 possible level combinations appear (each 5 times) instead of all 25 appearing 2 times.

## Evidence
Verified: L50 columns 1 vs 7 have 10 unique pairs (expected 25). Columns 2 vs 8 also have 10 unique pairs. Columns 1 vs 2 correctly have 25 unique pairs.

## Impact
The system uses L50 as the PRIMARY screening OA for 10 axes. With 10 factors assigned to columns 0-9, column pairs {1,7}, {2,8}, {3,9} are all within the assignment range. The 3 confounded pairs mean that 6 out of 10 factors have their main effects biased by the column-0 interaction. This is the core statistical module — biased main effects mean the Taguchi screening identifies wrong optimal levels.

## Fix
Replace with the published L50 table from Taguchi & Konishi (1987) or Hedayat et al. (1999). A valid L50(2^1×5^11) must have all column pairs balanced.

title: L54 OA construction produces confounded column pairs — same shifted-column pattern as L50
description:
## Bug
`_build_l54()` in `catalog.py:265` uses the same shifted-column pattern as L50: columns 14-25 are `(base[k] + a) % 3` where `a` is the 2-level column 0. This creates confounded column pairs between indices 1..13 and 14..25. Verified: columns 1 vs 14 have only 6 unique pairs (expected 9 for balanced 3×3).

## Impact
Lower impact than L50 since L54 is less commonly selected. But if used with 14+ factors, multiple confounded pairs would be in the assignment range.

## Fix
Use published L54 table from Taguchi & Konishi (1987).

title: predict_optimal prediction interval uses n instead of n_eff — interval is ~5.6x too narrow for 10-factor designs
description:
## Bug
`predict_optimal()` in `analysis.py:528` computes the prediction interval standard error as `se = sqrt(ms_error / n)` where `n = len(sn_ratios)` (total OA rows). The correct Taguchi formula uses n_eff:

```
n_eff = N / (1 + sum(df for all factors in additive model))
se = sqrt(ms_error / n_eff)
```

For a 10-factor design with ~4 levels each: n_eff = 50/(1+30) ≈ 1.61 vs n=50. The prediction interval is **5.6x too narrow**.

## Impact
`validate_confirmation()` uses this interval to check whether observed performance matches predicted. With a 5.6x-too-narrow interval, confirmation will almost always pass, even when the additive model is a poor fit. The confirmation phase becomes a rubber stamp instead of a validation gate.

## Fix
Change line 528 to compute n_eff from the design's factor degrees of freedom. The ANOVA result already has the necessary df values:

```python
total_df_factors = sum(f.df for f in anova_result.factors)
n_eff = n / (1 + total_df_factors)
se = math.sqrt(anova_result.ms_error / n_eff)
```

title: _group_refinement_scores maps single-variant trial scores to ALL matching rows — incorrect score attribution in refinement phase
description:
## Bug
`DOEPipeline._group_refinement_scores()` in `pipeline.py:117` builds a reverse mapping from variant names to design rows. A trial's `variant_name` is matched to ALL rows whose assignments contain that name as any level value. This means a trial for variant 'A' (axis_1) gets its score added to EVERY row where axis_1='A', regardless of the axis_2 level assigned to that row.

## Example
Design rows: row 1 = {axis_1:'A', axis_2:'X'}, row 2 = {axis_1:'A', axis_2:'Y'}
Trial variant_name='A' → score added to BOTH rows 1 and 2

## Impact
The refinement phase runs in 'full' mode (one variant per trial), then tries to reverse-map scores into OA rows for Taguchi analysis. The incorrect grouping means every row containing a given variant gets the same set of scores, making the per-row S/N ratios unreliable and the refinement ANOVA meaningless.

## Root cause
The method assumes a bijection between variant names and rows, but in a multi-factor design, each variant appears in multiple rows. Full-mode trials can't be meaningfully mapped back to OA rows without knowing the full factor combination.

## Fix
Either: (a) run refinement in Taguchi mode with a new design, or (b) compute main effects directly from trial scores grouped by variant/factor level without going through the row→S/N pipeline.

title: Pipeline resume reconstructs phases with trials=[] causing total_trials undercount in PipelineResult
description:
## Bug
`DOEPipeline.run()` in `pipeline.py:551-566` reconstructs completed phases from the DB with `trials=[]`. The `total_trials` aggregation on line 649 sums `len(phase.trials)` across all phases, producing 0 for any resumed/skipped phase. The resulting `PipelineResult.total_trials` undercounts the actual trials executed.

## Impact
Cosmetic: total_trials in the final report is wrong when resuming. Does not affect analysis since the trials are still in the DB.

## Fix
Either: (a) store total_trials per phase in phase_results DB and read it back during reconstruction, or (b) query the DB for trial count per run_id when reconstructing phases.

title: nominal_is_best S/N ratio uses population variance (n) instead of sample variance (n-1) — biased for small sample sizes
description:
## Bug
`compute_sn_ratios()` in `analysis.py:149` computes the nominal-is-best S/N ratio using population variance (divided by n) instead of sample variance (divided by n-1):

```python
variance = sum((y - mean_val) ** 2 for y in scores) / n  # should be / (n - 1)
```

The standard Taguchi formula (Phadke 1989) uses sample variance s².

## Impact
Low in practice: the primary quality type is larger_is_better (not nominal_is_best). For typical screening with n=3 reps per row, the bias is +1.76 dB. Since the bias is constant across all rows (same n), it doesn't affect relative rankings or ANOVA results. Only matters if absolute S/N values are interpreted or if different rows have different effective sample sizes due to error exclusion.

## Fix
Change line 149 to use `(n - 1)` denominator, with a guard for n=1:

```python
variance = sum((y - mean_val) ** 2 for y in scores) / max(n - 1, 1)
```

title: Add cross-model consistency testing as a first-class evaluation dimension

title: Add context window pressure testing (degradation curves)

This is critical because real-world agents often operate near context limits. The scale axis (6) only varies doc COUNT, not context PRESSURE relative to the model's window.

title: Add latency/cost-normalized scoring dimension
description: The framework records latency_seconds and cost per trial but doesn't incorporate them into optimization. A variant scoring 0.95 accuracy at 200K tokens and $0.50/query is worse than one scoring 0.90 at 20K tokens and $0.05/query. Need: (1) Pareto-frontier analysis: accuracy vs cost vs latency, (2) cost-efficiency composite scores (accuracy per dollar), (3) token-efficiency metrics (accuracy per 1K tokens), (4) Taguchi quality loss function that penalizes high-cost variants, (5) budget-constrained optimization: 'best format if I can only spend $X per query'. Currently the scoring module uses composite_score() that only weighs task types, completely ignoring economic factors. For production deployments this is the most important dimension after raw accuracy.

title: Add LLM-as-judge scoring to replace heuristic keyword matching
description: Every task type uses heuristic scoring: keyword matching, regex, fuzzy string comparison. This systematically undervalues correct answers phrased differently and overvalues keyword-stuffed wrong answers. The framework has a 2% judge sampling rate (JUDGE_SAMPLE_RATE=50) but doesn't use judge scores for optimization. Need: (1) LLM-as-judge as the PRIMARY scoring method (not 2% sample), (2) calibrate heuristic vs judge agreement rates per task type, (3) use judge scores in Taguchi S/N computation, (4) multi-judge consensus for high-stakes comparisons, (5) judge prompt templates per task type (fact extraction needs different rubric than code generation). The heuristic scoring systematically biases the framework — a variant that produces well-written natural language answers may score LOWER than one that produces keyword-rich but unhelpful responses. This undermines all results.
